story.title: Why your local LLM feels dumber than it is

draft:
Your on‑prem LLM isn’t dumb—it’s just missing the right context.  

I’ve been running a locally‑hosted LLaMA model and it often feels slower and less insightful than the cloud equivalents. The architecture is identical; the difference lies in the surrounding scaffolding.  

- Quantization saves RAM but trims precision in the tail of the distribution, hurting nuanced reasoning.  
- Absent a well‑crafted system prompt or tuned temperature, the model falls back to safe, generic answers.  
- Adding a lightweight retrieval‑augmented generation layer supplies the external knowledge that cloud services pre‑index.  

For me the key is to treat a local LLM as a component, not a finished product. A few minutes of prompt engineering, sampling tweaks, and optional post‑processing can close most of the perceived intelligence gap.
